213: Threshold CBM-patent status determination: the Board applied an incorrect 'incidental to' or 'complementary to' legal standard in deciding whether the '752 patent is a covered business method patent, so the institution/threshold ruling was vacated and remanded.

We hold that the Board's reliance on whether the patent claims activities "incidental to" or "complementary to" a financial activity as the legal standard to determine whether a patent is a CBM patent was not in accordance with law.
302: Institution, time bar under 315(b): Board's determination that Apple's IPR petitions were not time-barred is unreviewable because it relates to institution under 314(d).

We thus hold that 35 U.S.C. § 314(d) prohibits this court from reviewing the Board's determination to initiate IPR proceedings based on its assessment of the time-bar of § 315(b), even if such assessment is reconsidered during the merits phase of proceedings and restated as part of the Board's final written decision.
319: Reviewability of the Board's institution of an IPR under the 35 U.S.C. §315(b) one-year time bar; the court held §314(d) bars review under Achates and Wi-Fi One, so the institution stands.
We therefore once more dismiss CTC's appeal for lack of jurisdiction.
461: Section 315(b) time bar and privity: Board found Broadcom not in privity with time-barred district court litigants; court held the time-bar ruling unreviewable under 35 U.S.C. 314(d) and Achates.
We see nothing in the Cuozzo decision that suggests Achates has been implicitly overruled.
675: Whether the same Board panel that instituted IPR may render the final decision (institution/final decision combination, due process and statutory authority)

We disagree with Ethicon and conclude that, where, as here, there are no other separate procedural-fairness infirmities alleged, the PTO's assignment of the institution and final decisions to one panel of the Board does not violate due process under governing Supreme Court precedent.
725: Scope of the final written decision: the Board need not address in its final written decision claims challenged in the petition but not instituted for IPR, following Synopsys.
We reject SAS's argument that the Board must address all claims challenged in an IPR petition in its final written decision.
959: Reviewability of Board institution of IPR; court held it lacks jurisdiction to review whether the §315(b) time bar was properly rejected at institution under §314(d)
Review of whether the PTO properly instituted inter partes review is forbidden by § 314(d).
1493: Threshold ruling that the '573 and '440 patents are covered business method patents, so the Board's authority to review them was proper
We affirm the Board's determination that the '573 and '440 patents qualify as CBM patents.
1647: Whether the Board had to consider the non-instituted grounds deemed redundant after finding claim 11 patentable over the instituted ground; court held the Board was not required to address grounds not instituted and upheld the subset-of-grounds regulation, 37 C.F.R. § 42.108.
Under the IPR framework, Congress did not require that once the PTO institutes a proceeding, all grounds in the underlying petition must be considered.
1841: CBM eligibility: whether the challenged claims are covered business method patents that do not claim a technological invention, so the Board could conduct CBM review
We therefore affirm the Board's conclusion that the challenged claims of the Blue Calypso Patents meet the statutory definition of CBM patent.
2183: Scope of final written decision: whether the Board must address every challenged claim after claim-by-claim institution; held no requirement to address all claims
In summary, we find no statutory requirement that the Board's final decision address every claim raised in a petition for inter partes review.
2185: Section 315(b) time bar and real party in interest ruling; non-appealable under section 314(d) per Achates
This issue is not appealable pursuant to § 314(d).
2268: Reviewability of the Board's decision not to institute IPR on redundancy grounds under 35 U.S.C. §314(d); court held it cannot review the institution decision and related challenges to the scope of institution.
Accordingly, we cannot review the Board's refusal to institute IPR on redundancy grounds, and we find that the final written decision meets the agency's obligations under the APA.
2385: Institution of IPR and §315(b) time bar challenge; court declined review of institution decision under §314(d)
Because CTC's challenge amounts to a "statutory interpretation dispute," dismissal is appropriate.
2450: Reviewability of the Board's decision to institute inter partes reexamination after the requester asked that its request be denied; court held it lacked authority to review the institution decision because a request and requester were present.

Because a request and a requester were present, the Board acted within its statutory authority when it decided to institute reexamination in this case, and we lack authority to further consider the prudence or propriety of the Board's institution decision.
3776: Whether the Board improperly shifted the burden of proof to the patent owner to disprove a motivation to combine; court held no improper burden shifting
We reject Essity's suggestion that the Board's statements refuting Essity's evidence amount to shifting the burden to Essity to disprove a motivation to combine.
3940: Institution scope under SAS: the court remanded so the Board can consider non-instituted claims 17-26 and 29-31 and non-instituted grounds for claims 27, 28, and 32-35.
We remand, however, for the Board to consider whether non-instituted claims 17–26 and 29–31 are unpatentable and whether claims 27, 28, 32–35 are unpatentable based on the non-instituted grounds.
3983: Section 315(b) time bar: the Board's final written decision in IPR2016-01589 was vacated because the inter partes review was time-barred, and the court remanded for dismissal.
We vacate the Board's final written decision in IPR2016-01589, and we remand for dismissal of the inter partes review as time-barred under 35 U.S.C. § 315(b).
4104: Joinder of Apple to the IPRs under 315(b)-(c); court found no prejudice to VirnetX and did not decide whether joinder was permitted
At this stage in the proceedings, we see no prejudice in Apple's continued involvement, but we leave open the question of whether prejudice could arise later.
4105: Real party in interest: substantial evidence supports Board finding that Mangrove Partners is not a real party in interest
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Mangrove Partners is not a real party in interest.
4260: Real-party-in-interest determination under 35 U.S.C. § 312(a)(2) in IPR institution; Board's determination held unreviewable under § 314(d)

we hold that ESIP's challenge to the Board's "real parties in interest" determination "raises 'an ordinary dispute about the application of' an institution-related statute," and that § 314(d) precludes our review of that determination.
4296: Institution: the Board instituted IPR on fewer than all challenged claims; UUSI did not show the error was harmless, and the court remanded for the Board to consider claims 37-39.
in light of the disposition of the above issues UUSI has not shown that the Board's error in instituting IPR on less than all challenged claims was harmless
4534: Section 315(b) time bar: the IPR petition against the '319 patent was time-barred because the earlier infringement complaint, though voluntarily dismissed without prejudice, still triggers the bar, so institution was improper

because the section 315(b) time-bar applies when the underlying complaint alleging infringement has been voluntarily dismissed without prejudice, the Board erred in instituting the IPR challenging the '319 patent.
4560: CBM eligibility for review: the PTAB's finding that the patents are not excluded by the technological invention exception and are eligible for CBM review, affirmed.
We do not detect error in the PTAB's findings or reasoning and, therefore, conclude that the Patents-in-Suit are CBM patents eligible for review.
4787: Real-party-in-interest determination under 35 U.S.C. 315(a)(1) made at institution is unreviewable after Thryv; Toyota's motion to terminate and remand to dismiss was denied
Thryv compels the conclusion that the real party in interest determination under section 315(a)(1), which is decided at the institution stage, is unreviewable by this court.
4796: Reviewability of institution: the court declined to review the merits of a finding made only in the institution decision.
We need not address Merck's argument because our review of Board proceedings does not include review of the merits of the institution decision.
4939: Real-party-in-interest and §315(b) time bar: Board's RPI analysis erred, including allocation of the burden of persuasion; decisions vacated and remanded with the ultimate burden on the petitioner.
Because we hold that the Board erred in its real-party-in-interest analysis, we vacate its decisions and remand for proceedings consistent with this opinion.
5060: Section 315(b) time bar: the Board's final written decisions in the two IPRs were vacated because the IPRs were time-barred, and the court remanded for dismissal.
We vacate the Board's final written decisions in IPR2016-00995 and IPR2016-01597, and we remand for dismissal of those inter partes reviews as time-barred under 35 U.S.C. § 315(b).
5083: Same-party joinder under 35 U.S.C. 315(c): Board allowed Facebook to be joined to its own already-instituted IPRs; held improper, claims added through joinder vacated.

we hold that the Board's joinder decisions, which allowed Facebook to join itself to a proceeding in which it was already a party, and to add otherwise time-barred issues to the IPRs, were improper under § 315(c).
5084: Joinder of new issues/claims (including time-barred claims) into existing IPRs under 315(c); held not authorized, claims 19, 22-25 and 203, 209, 215, 221, 477, 482, 487, 492 vacated.
the clear and unambiguous language of § 315(c) does not authorize same-party joinder, and also does not authorize joinder of new issues, including issues that would otherwise be time-barred.
5230: Whether the Federal Reserve Banks are 'persons' under the AIA who may petition for CBM review, so the Board had authority to decide the petitions; court held the Banks are persons.
we hold that the Banks are "persons" who may petition for post-issuance review under the AIA.
5373: Time bar under 35 U.S.C. 315(b) and real party in interest: the Board applied an unduly narrow test for whether Salesforce was a real party in interest and misallocated the burden, so the time-bar determination was vacated.

we conclude that the Board applied an unduly restrictive test for determining whether a person or entity is a 'real party in interest' within the meaning of § 315(b) and failed to consider the entirety of the evidentiary record in assessing whether § 315(b) barred institution of these IPRs.
5482: Whether the Board erred in instituting the PGR under the 'reasonable likelihood' rather than the 'more likely than not' standard; the court found no error because the Board made findings under the correct standard and the references to reasonable likelihood were harmless.

Thus, even if this issue were appealable, we would find that the Board did not err in instituting the PGR because it made explicit determinations under the correct, 'more likely than not' standard; references to 'a reasonable likelihood' were harmless.
5556: SAS-based remand to the Board to consider grounds that were not instituted in IPR2017-00118.
Although we chose not to terminate the appeal as to IPR No. 2017-00118, we now remand to the Board to consider the non-instituted grounds.
5606: Whether the PTAB properly denied the patent owner's motion to terminate IPR under 35 U.S.C. 315(a)(1) based on real-party-in-interest status of Amazon; the court found the patent owner did not show Amazon was an RPI.
Accordingly, GEMSA did not meet its burden to "produce some evidence that tends to show that [Amazon] should be named a real party in interest."
5629: Reviewability of the Board's priority date determination, which relates only to a non-instituted ground (Touboul) and is unreviewable as a challenge to the institution decision
We hold that PAN cannot appeal this determination because it is only relevant to the Board’s decision not to institute inter partes review.
5635: Section 315(b) time bar: whether privity and real-party-in-interest relationships arising after filing but before institution count, and whether Fairchild, a time-barred party, was an RPI when the IPR was instituted. The court held the IPR time-barred and vacated the final written decision.
we hold that this IPR was time-barred by § 315(b) because Fairchild was an RPI at the time the IPR was instituted, even though it was not an RPI at the time the petition was filed.
5795: Section 315(b) time bar on IPR institution: whether the IPR petition was filed more than one year after service of an infringement complaint. Court held the petition was not time-barred and found no error in the Board's decision to institute, though it corrected the Board's view that it lacked authority to determine service.
we discern no error in the Board's decision to institute the IPR.
6050: Issue preclusion barring Apple's obviousness and non-joinder invalidity challenges based on prior litigation (framed as preclusion; coded as validity-related preclusion ruling favoring patent owner)
We therefore affirm the district court's determination that Apple is precluded from raising these invalidity challenges in the present case.
6103: Scope of Board institution: the Board instituted IPR on fewer than all challenged claims and grounds in the -00151 IPR and issued a final written decision on the non-instituted claims, so the court vacated and remanded for a decision consistent with SAS Institute.

Because the -00151 IPR FWD addresses fewer than all claims challenged in Palo Alto's petition to institute inter partes review in the -00151 IPR, and because Palo Alto has not waived its objection to the Board's failure to address the non-instituted claims, we vacate and remand to allow the Board to issue a Final Written Decision consistent with SAS.
6175: Real party-in-interest determination under §312(a)(2) and reviewability under §314(d); mandamus review rejected
we reject Fall Line's contention that the present appeal justifies mandamus review.
6259: Section 315(b) time bar: privity and real party in interest; whether the Board applied the correct legal standard and whether petition is time-barred
The majority affirms the Board's decision that Broadcom's petition is not time barred under § 315(b).
6263: Section 315(b) one-year time bar: the Board lacked authority to institute IPR because the petition was filed more than a year after service of a complaint alleging infringement, even though the complaint was involuntarily dismissed without prejudice.
The Board lacked authority to institute review. Accordingly, we vacate the Board's final written decision, and we remand for the Board to dismiss the IPR.
6269: Section 315(b) time bar: the court held ION was not a privy or real party in interest of PGS, so the IPR petitions were not time-barred.
Accordingly, the petitions are not barred under 35 U.S.C. § 315(b).
6289: Real-party-in-interest and time bar: Board permitted petitioner to amend its RPI disclosure to add Merck & Co. without changing the petition filing date, so the §315(b) time bar did not apply.
we conclude that the Board did not err in allowing MSD to amend its disclosures to add MCI as a real party in interest without altering the petition's filing date.
6311: Institution reviewability under the 35 U.S.C. § 314(d) No Appeal clause: the court held the challenge that the Board exceeded its authority by instituting review on an unasserted ground is an unappealable institution decision
We agree with the Director that Lone Star's challenge is directed to the Board's institution decision, which is not appealable.
6463: Board's partial institution of IPR on only two of four grounds was foreclosed by SAS; court remanded for the Board to consider the non-instituted grounds.
SAS forecloses this type of partial institution.
6496: Section 315(c) joinder: Board improperly allowed Facebook to join itself to its own instituted IPRs and to add time-barred new claims through joinder; final written decisions vacated as to joined claims.
we hold that the clear and unambiguous language of § 315(c) does not authorize same-party joinder or joinder of new issues.
6714: Inventorship/prior-art status of mAb 6-2 disclosure under §102(e) raised in Sanofi cross-appeal; court declined to reach and dismissed cross-appeal as moot
Because we affirm the Board's invalidity judgment in the other IPR, which implicates the same claims, it is unnecessary to reach this issue.
6797: CBM eligibility: Board's determination that the '556 patent is a covered business method patent and not a technological invention under AIA 18(d) and 37 C.F.R. 42.301(b), reviewed for arbitrary and capricious reasoning.
We conclude the Board's reasoning that the '556 patent is a CBM patent was not arbitrary and capricious.
6833: Board's institution of IPR on an obviousness ground (SMIL 1.0 in view of Hua) that the petition did not advance; held the Board erred in instituting on a ground not in the petition.
We hold that the Board erred by instituting inter partes review based on a combination of prior art references not advanced in Google's petition.
6844: Reviewability of the Board's threshold determination that the '842 patent qualifies for CBM review (not a technological invention); held nonappealable under 35 U.S.C. 324(e) and Thryv.
We therefore are precluded from reviewing SIPCO's challenge to that threshold determination.
6875: Whether Bank of America is a real party in interest under 312(a)(2); review barred by 314(d) under Thryv and ESIP, so the Board's no-RPI ruling stands
we hold that § 314(d) precludes our review of the Board's decision that Bank of America is not a real party in interest.
6963: Section 315(b) one-year time bar: whether service of a complaint later voluntarily dismissed without prejudice triggers the time bar, and whether the petition is time-barred as a unitary petition by all petitioners
we conclude that a defendant served with a complaint as part of a civil action that is voluntarily dismissed without prejudice remains "served" with the "complaint."
7139: CBM eligibility threshold: whether the patent is excluded from CBM review as a technological invention under 37 C.F.R. 42.301(b); court reversed the Board's finding, favoring the patent owner.

Because SIPCO's claims combine certain communication elements in a particular way to address a specific technical problem with a specific technical solution, we reverse the Board's finding that the patent does not satisfy the second part of its technological invention regulation.
7140: CBM eligibility threshold: whether claims 3 and 4 recite an apparatus used in the practice of a financial product or service under AIA 18(d)(1); court affirmed the Board, favoring the petitioner.
We therefore do not find that the Board abused its discretion when it determined that the claimed apparatus was used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service.
7165: Institution of inter partes review: the Board erred by instituting review on less than all claims and grounds in the petition, so the remainder of the final written decision was vacated and remanded for review of all claims and grounds.
Under SAS, however, the Board erred by instituting review on less than all claims and grounds included in Alere's petition.
7167: Board's alleged departure from the grounds asserted in the IPR petition (whether petition fairly contemplated combination of all three references)
We see no sufficient reason to disturb the Board's decision on these grounds.
8211: Challenge to Black Swamp's joinder in IPR2015-01047 held forfeited for failure to raise in prior appeal.
Accordingly, the issue is forfeited. See, e.g., Vivint v. Alarm.com Inc.
8216: Real-party-in-interest and privity: Board's finding that LG is not an RPI or privy of Facebook, so LG is not estopped, was affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
The Board's determination that LG is not an RPI or privy of Facebook is supported by substantial evidence.
9964: PGR eligibility: Board found the '979 patent eligible for post-grant review because the claims could not claim priority to the pre-AIA application for lack of written description support in the priority chain; affirmed as part of the threshold analysis (court treated eligibility as rising or falling with the §112(b) issues).
we, like TWW, treat the issue of eligibility for postgrant review as rising or falling with the § 112(b) issues.
10534: Scope of the IPR petition: whether the Board abused its discretion in declining to treat the petition as challenging claim 18 for obviousness over Obelix and Skillen, which is a petition-particularity/threshold ruling

We are unpersuaded that the Board abused its discretion in declining to interpret Microsoft's petition as challenging claim 18 over Obelix and Skillen based on such tenuous connections in Microsoft's petition.
10779: Board's finding that Microsoft's petition insufficiently pleaded unpatentability of claims 29-47 of the '115 patent (particularity requirement; reply-introduced claim differences)
We affirm the Board's determination that Microsoft insufficiently pleaded the unpatentability of claims 29–47.
10780: Board's finding that Microsoft's petition did not sufficiently demonstrate particularity for grounds against claims 86-89 of the '115 patent; cross-reference to claim 1 discussion held an abuse of discretion

Accordingly, we reverse the Board's finding that Microsoft's petition did not sufficiently demonstrate with particularity the evidentiary support for the grounds for the challenge to claims 86–89 of the ’115 patent
11882: Reviewability of the Board's and Director's decision not to apply interference estoppel to institution of the IPR; held unreviewable under 35 U.S.C. § 314(d) as within the institution determination.

we conclude that the decision is within the general rule of unreviewability, and, to the extent the Supreme Court's decision in Cuozzo Speed Technologies, LLC v. Lee might allow inquiry into whether the Board engaged in "shenanigans" not in accordance with law, 579 U.S. 261, 275 (2016), there were no shenanigans here
12118: Reviewability of institution: Hafeman's challenge based on LG's alleged violation of the Sotera stipulation was held barred by 35 U.S.C. § 314(d) as a challenge to the institution decision, so the appeal on that issue was dismissed.
Accordingly, Ms. Hafeman's challenge is barred from judicial review by § 314(d), and we must dismiss this portion of her appeal.
12722: Real-party-in-interest challenge (whether Roambee had to be named under 312(a)(2)); rejected by reference to a companion appeal, leaving the Board's determination for the petitioner.
we reject the portions of FedEx's appeal challenging the Board's real party in interest determination.
13047: Due process challenge to Board IPR decisions based on Director Vidal's alleged conflict of interest and APJ pecuniary interest; claim that APJs were biased toward unpatentability
UTL has not established that the APJs had an unconstitutional financial interest in deciding the IPRs in favor of unpatentability, such that its due process rights were violated.
14933: Reviewability of the Board's reconsideration and institution of IPR; 35 U.S.C. 314(d) bars review of EBS's challenge to the stay and institution
Section 314(d) bars us from reviewing the Director's decision to institute an inter partes review.
15082: Real party in interest under 35 U.S.C. § 312(a)(2) (whether Roambee had to be named); court rejected FedEx's challenge to the Board's real-party-in-interest determination.
Accordingly, as in that case, we reject the part of FedEx's appeal challenging the Board's real party-in-interest determination.
